3.2 A student does not need to have a specific diagnosis label to receive accommodations. What matters is the presence of a disability and the need for an accommodation to access university programs.

3.3 Temporary conditions, such as a broken arm or short-term illness, are not typically considered disabilities under this policy. However, students with temporary conditions may contact the office to discuss short-term assistance options.

3.4 The university does not discriminate against students on the basis of disability in admission, access to programs, or employment. This policy is consistent with applicable federal and state laws.

Section 4. Documentation Requirements

4.1 Students are encouraged to submit documentation that describes the nature of the disability and the functional limitations it presents. Documentation helps the office understand how the disability affects the student in the academic environment.

4.2 Acceptable documentation may include:

a. A letter from a licensed medical professional, psychologist, or other qualified evaluator;
b. A prior educational evaluation, such as an IEP or 504 plan;
c. Records from a previous school’s disability services office;
d. Other reliable information, such as a detailed self-report, when appropriate.

4.3 Documentation should include, when available:

a. A description of the diagnostic criteria used;
b. A summary of the evaluation or assessment results;
c. A description of current functional limitations;
d. Recommendations for accommodations, if any.

4.4 The office may request additional information if the submitted documentation is incomplete or insufficient to determine eligibility. The student will be notified in writing of any additional information needed.

Maplewood State University has_accommodation_policy_version 2025-01-01 date. Record status: current.

4.5 All documentation is kept confidential and is shared only with those individuals who have a legitimate need to know, as permitted by law.

Section 5. Application Steps

5.1 Step 1: Submit an Intake Form. Students begin the process by completing the online intake form available on the OAR website. The form asks for basic information and a description of the requested accommodations.

5.2 Step 2: Submit Documentation. Students should upload or deliver their documentation to the office. Documentation may be submitted at the same time as the intake form or later.

5.3 Step 3: Meet with an Accessibility Coordinator. After receiving the intake form and documentation, the office will schedule an interactive meeting. This meeting is an opportunity to discuss the student’s needs, the impact of the disability, and potential accommodations.

5.4 Step 4: Receive an Accommodation Letter. If accommodations are approved, the office will issue an accommodation letter. This letter lists the approved accommodations and is sent to the student electronically. The student is responsible for sharing the letter with their instructors.

5.5 Step 5: Implement and Review. Accommodations begin when the student shares the letter with faculty. Students are encouraged to review their accommodations each semester and request adjustments if needed.

5.6 Students may apply for accommodations at any time during their enrollment. However, accommodations are not retroactive. It is recommended that students begin the process as early as possible, especially for housing or testing accommodations.

Section 6. Types of Accommodations
Section 7. Office Hours, Location, and Scheduling

7.1 The Office of Accessibility Resources is located in the Student Services Building, Room 210. The entrance is on the north side of the building, facing the parking garage. A ramp is available at the main entrance, and the office is accessible by elevator.

7.2 Office hours: Office of Accessibility Resources office_hours Monday-Friday 9:00-17:00 hours. Record status: current. The office is closed on university holidays and during scheduled staff training days. A list of closure dates is posted on the office door and on the OAR website.

7.3 Walk-in hours are available Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM for quick questions, document drop-off, and scheduling assistance. No appointment is needed for walk-in visits during this time. The rest of the day is reserved for scheduled appointments.

7.4 To schedule an appointment with an Accessibility Coordinator, students may:

a. Call the office at (555) 214-8890 during business hours;
b. Email oar@maplewood.edu with a preferred date and time; or
c. Use the online scheduling portal available through the OAR website.

7.5 Appointments are typically available within five business days. During peak periods (the first two weeks of each semester), appointment availability may be limited. Students who need an urgent appointment should call the office and speak with the front desk staff.

7.6 If a student cannot attend a scheduled appointment, they should cancel at least 24 hours in advance by phone or through the online portal. Missed appointments without prior cancellation may result in a wait for the next available slot.

7.7 Students who need communication access services (such as sign language interpreters or CART) for their appointment should request this when scheduling. The office asks for at least five business days' notice to arrange these services.

7.8 The office is equipped with an adjustable-height desk in the meeting rooms. Students who use wheelchairs or other mobility devices can access all consultation rooms. If a student needs a different meeting space, the coordinator will arrange an alternative location.

Section 8. Confidentiality and Record-Keeping

8.1 The Office of Accessibility Resources maintains records for each student who applies for or receives accommodations. These records include the intake form, documentation, correspondence, accommodation letters, and notes from meetings with coordinators.

8.2 All records are kept confidential and are stored in a secure electronic system with access limited to OAR staff. Paper records, when they exist, are kept in locked filing cabinets in a restricted area of the office.

8.3 Information is shared only with individuals who have a legitimate need to know, as permitted by law. This includes:

a. Instructors who receive the accommodation letter;
b. Other university offices (such as Housing or Dining) when an accommodation requires their involvement; and
c. Designated university officials who are involved in grievance or complaint processes.

8.4 The office does not disclose a student's disability diagnosis or documentation to faculty or other university staff. The accommodation letter describes the approved accommodations but does not include diagnostic information.

8.5 Students may request a copy of their own records at any time. Requests should be made in writing to the office. The office will provide copies within ten business days.
Section 9. Standard Approval Durations

9.1 Each accommodation is approved for a standard period of time, after which the student must renew in order to continue receiving the accommodation. The standard approval duration depends on the type of accommodation and is listed in the table below.

9.2 Standard approval durations:

9.3 The Extended Exam Time Accommodation has a standard approval duration of one semester. Record status: current. This is the current standard and applies to all students approved for this accommodation, regardless of when they first received it.

9.4 Students who are approved for an accommodation with a one-semester duration must submit a renewal request before the end of the semester in which the accommodation is active. The office recommends submitting the renewal request at least two weeks before the end of the semester to avoid a gap in services.

9.5 Renewal requests are reviewed by the same coordinator who approved the original accommodation. In most cases, the renewal is approved without additional documentation if the student's situation has not changed. The coordinator may request updated documentation if there has been a significant change in the student's condition or circumstances.

9.6 Students who do not submit a renewal request by the deadline will have their accommodation discontinued at the end of the semester. The office will send a reminder email two weeks before the end of the semester to students with expiring accommodations. It is the student's responsibility to check their university email account and respond to this reminder.

9.7 If an accommodation is discontinued due to non-renewal, the student may reapply at any time. The reapplication process is the same as the initial application process and may require new documentation. The office cannot guarantee that the accommodation will be approved again if the student's circumstances have changed.

9.8 Students who have an accommodation with a two-semester duration must also renew, but less frequently. The renewal process for these accommodations is the same as for one-semester accommodations, but the renewal request is due before the end of the second semester of the approval period.

9.9 The office will review the standard approval durations each year. The review takes place in the spring semester, and any changes are announced in the fall semester. The standard durations listed in this handbook are current as of the version date on the cover of this handbook.

Section 10. Renewal Process

10.1 The renewal process is designed to be simple and straightforward. Students do not need to meet with a coordinator to renew an accommodation unless the coordinator requests a meeting.

10.2 To renew an accommodation, a student should:

a. Log in to the online portal;
b. Select the accommodation they wish to renew;
c. Confirm that their information is still accurate; and
d. Submit the renewal request.

10.3 The student will receive a confirmation email when the renewal request is received. The coordinator will review the request and send a decision within five business days.

10.4 If the renewal is approved, the student will receive a new accommodation letter. The letter will list the accommodation and the new approval period. The student should share the letter with their instructors at the beginning of the next semester.

10.5 If the renewal is denied, the coordinator will explain the reason in writing. The student may appeal the decision through the grievance process described in Section 11.
Section 11. Grievance and Appeal Process

11.1 The office is committed to resolving concerns fairly and promptly. Most concerns can be
resolved through an informal conversation with the student's coordinator. Students are encouraged
to begin there before filing a formal grievance.

11.2 A formal grievance may be filed when a student believes that:

a. an accommodation request was denied without proper review;
b. an accommodation was not implemented by an instructor or department;
c. the office failed to respond within the timeframes described in this handbook; or
d. the student experienced retaliation for requesting or using an accommodation.

11.3 To file a formal grievance, a student should submit a written statement to the office by
email or through the online portal. The statement should describe the issue, the steps already
taken to resolve it, and the outcome the student is seeking. Grievances should be filed within
30 calendar days of the event or of the student's awareness of the event, whichever is later.

11.4 Upon receiving a formal grievance, the office will send an acknowledgment within three
business days. The acknowledgment will include the name of the grievance coordinator assigned to
the case and an estimated timeline for review.

11.5 The grievance coordinator will review the grievance, gather relevant records, and consult
with the student and any involved instructors or staff. The coordinator may also speak with other
offices as needed. The review will generally be completed within 20 business days of the
acknowledgment.

11.6 The grievance coordinator will issue a written decision. The decision will state whether the
grievance was upheld, denied, or resolved through a negotiated agreement. If the grievance is
upheld, the decision will include the corrective action to be taken and the timeline for
completion.

11.7 If the student is not satisfied with the grievance coordinator's decision, they may appeal
in writing within 10 business days of receiving the decision. The appeal should explain why the
student believes the decision was incorrect or incomplete.

11.8 Appeals are reviewed by the Director of Accessibility Resources, who will issue a final
decision within 15 business days of receiving the appeal. The Director's decision is final and is
not subject to further appeal within the office.

11.9 Throughout the grievance process, the student may be accompanied by a support person of
their choice. The support person may attend meetings but may not speak on the student's behalf
unless the student requests assistance with communication access.

11.10 The office will maintain records of all grievances and their outcomes for five years.
These records are confidential and shared only as required by law or with the student's written
permission.

Section 12. Campus Disability Advisory Committee

12.1 The Campus Disability Advisory Committee (CDAC) advises the office on policy, programs, and
accessibility priorities. The committee includes students, faculty, and staff, and meets at least
twice per semester during the academic year.

12.2 CDAC membership is open. Students who are interested in serving should contact the office
by email. Faculty and staff members are appointed by their respective governance bodies.

12.3 The committee reviews the annual accommodation data summary, discusses emerging issues, and
may propose changes to office policy. Proposals from CDAC are advisory. The Director of
Accessibility Resources decides whether to adopt, modify, or decline a proposal.
Section 13. Frequently Asked Questions

13.1 Who is eligible for accommodations?

Any student with a documented disability that substantially limits one or more major life
activities may be eligible. Documentation must be current and provided by a qualified
professional. The office reviews each request on an individual basis. A diagnosis alone does
not automatically result in accommodations; the impact of the disability in the academic
setting is also considered.

13.2 How do I request accommodations?

Submit the Accommodation Request Form through the student portal. Attach your documentation.
The office will review your request and contact you to schedule an intake meeting. You do not
need to request accommodations before the semester begins, but early requests allow more time
for implementation.

13.3 How long does the review process take?

The office aims to review complete requests within 10 business days of receipt. If
documentation is incomplete or unclear, the office will contact you for additional
information. The timeline restarts once all materials are received.

13.4 Can I receive accommodations for online classes?

Yes. Many accommodations apply to online courses, including extended time on quizzes,
captioning for recorded lectures, and alternative formats for course materials. Discuss your
specific needs with your accessibility specialist.

13.5 Are accommodations retroactive?

No. Accommodations begin after your accommodation plan is approved and you have notified your
instructors. The office cannot provide retroactive accommodations for past assignments or
exams.

13.6 What if my instructor does not follow my accommodation plan?

Contact the office as soon as possible. The office will help resolve the issue with the
instructor. If the issue is not resolved informally, you may file a grievance under Section
11 of this handbook.

13.7 Do I need to request accommodations every semester?

No. Once your accommodation plan is approved, it remains in effect until you graduate, take a
leave of absence, or request changes. You are responsible for notifying your instructors each
semester that you are using accommodations.

13.8 Can I change my accommodation plan?

Yes. You may request changes at any time by contacting your accessibility specialist. Changes
may require updated documentation. The office will review requested changes and notify you of
the decision within 10 business days.

13.9 What if I am not satisfied with a decision about my accommodations?

You may discuss your concerns with your accessibility specialist or the Director of
Accessibility Resources. If the issue is not resolved, you may file a grievance under Section
11. You may also contact the U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights at any time.

13.10 Are accommodations confidential?

Yes. The office maintains all records as confidential. Information is shared only with your
written permission or as required by law. Instructors receive a notification letter that lists
your accommodations, but not your diagnosis or documentation.

Section 14. Glossary of Terms

14.1 Accommodation Plan: A written document listing the specific accommodations a student is
eligible to receive. The plan is developed in the intake meeting and updated as needed.

14.2 Accessibility Specialist: The staff member assigned to a student to coordinate
accommodations and provide support.

14.3 Auxiliary Aids and Services: Tools and supports that enable equal access, including
sign language interpreters, captioning, assistive technology, and note-taking services.

Dear Sofia,

We are pleased to confirm that your accommodation plan has been approved by the Office of Accessibility Resources (OAR). This letter outlines the accommodations approved for you, the effective dates, and the steps you need to take to ensure they are implemented properly in each of your courses.

Approved Accommodations

The following accommodations are approved for the Fall 2025 semester:

1. **Extended Testing Time** – Time and one-half (1.5x) on all exams and quizzes in courses where you have submitted a Testing Request Form. This includes in-class tests, online assessments, and final exams.  
2. **Reduced-Distraction Testing Environment** – Access to the OAR Testing Center for exams that require a quiet, low-distraction setting. You may also request this environment for in-class exams if your instructor is able to proctor in a separate room.

These accommodations are based on the documentation you submitted to OAR and are designed to provide equal access to your coursework. Please note that these accommodations are not retroactive, as stated in the previous section of this letter.

How to Use Your Accommodations

To ensure your accommodations are in place for each course, please follow the steps below:

- **Log in to the OAR Student Portal** at oarportal.stateuniversity.edu to review your approved accommodations and confirm that your current course list is accurate. If any courses are missing from your list, contact OAR within five business days of receiving this letter.  
- **Submit a Testing Request Form** for each exam or quiz at least three business days before the scheduled assessment. This form is available in the OAR Student Portal. You will receive a confirmation email once your request is processed.  
- **For note-taking services**, check the portal each day after your classes to see if notes have been posted. If you do not see notes within 24 hours of a class session, please contact the Note-Taking Coordinator, Dana Whitfield, at d.whitfield@stateuniversity.edu or call the OAR front desk.  
- **For preferential seating**, speak with each instructor during the first week of classes to arrange your seating. OAR does not notify instructors about seating preferences; this is something you will coordinate directly.

We recommend that you follow up with each instructor to confirm they have received the notification and to discuss any course-specific logistics, such as how extended time will be handled for online exams or how to arrange for the reduced-distraction environment.
Renewal and Changes to Your Accommodations

Your approved accommodations are valid for the current semester as listed in this letter. If you wish to continue receiving accommodations in a future semester, you must request a renewal through the OAR Student Portal. Renewal requests should be submitted no later than the third week of the semester prior to the one in which you need accommodations. For example, if you need accommodations for the Fall semester, submit your renewal request by the third week of the Spring semester. This timeline allows OAR sufficient time to review your request and notify your instructors before the start of the term.

Appeals must be submitted in writing within fifteen business days of the denial notice. The appeal should include a statement explaining why you believe the decision was incorrect and any supporting documentation. Section 11. Grievance and Appeal Process

11.1 The office is committed to resolving concerns fairly and promptly. Most concerns can be
resolved through an informal conversation with the student's coordinator. Students are encouraged
to begin there before filing a formal grievance.

11.2 A formal grievance may be filed when a student believes that:

a. an accommodation request was denied without proper review;
b. an accommodation was not implemented by an instructor or department;
c. the office failed to respond within the timeframes described in this handbook; or
d. the student experienced retaliation for requesting or using an accommodation.

11.3 To file a formal grievance, a student should submit a written statement to the office by
email or through the online portal. The statement should describe the issue, the steps already
taken to resolve it, and the outcome the student is seeking. Grievances should be filed within
30 calendar days of the event or of the student's awareness of the event, whichever is later.

11.4 Upon receiving a formal grievance, the office will send an acknowledgment within three
business days. The acknowledgment will include the name of the grievance coordinator assigned to
the case and an estimated timeline for review.

11.5 The grievance coordinator will review the grievance, gather relevant records, and consult
with the student and any involved instructors or staff. The coordinator may also speak with other
offices as needed. The review will generally be completed within 20 business days of the
acknowledgment.

11.6 The grievance coordinator will issue a written decision. The decision will state whether the
grievance was upheld, denied, or resolved through a negotiated agreement. If the grievance is
upheld, the decision will include the corrective action to be taken and the timeline for
completion.

11.7 If the student is not satisfied with the grievance coordinator's decision, they may appeal
in writing within 10 business days of receiving the decision. The appeal should explain why the
student believes the decision was incorrect or incomplete.

11.8 Appeals are reviewed by the Director of Accessibility Resources, who will issue a final
decision within 15 business days of receiving the appeal. The Director's decision is final and is
not subject to further appeal within the office.

11.9 Throughout the grievance process, the student may be accompanied by a support person of
their choice. The support person may attend meetings but may not speak on the student's behalf
unless the student requests assistance with communication access.

11.10 The office will maintain records of all grievances and their outcomes for five years.
These records are confidential and shared only as required by law or with the student's written
permission.

Section 12. Campus Disability Advisory Committee

12.1 The Campus Disability Advisory Committee (CDAC) advises the office on policy, programs, and
accessibility priorities. The committee includes students, faculty, and staff, and meets at least
twice per semester during the academic year.

12.2 CDAC membership is open. Students who are interested in serving should contact the office
by email. Faculty and staff members are appointed by their respective governance bodies.

12.3 The committee reviews the annual accommodation data summary, discusses emerging issues, and
may propose changes to office policy. Proposals from CDAC are advisory. The Director of
Accessibility Resources decides whether to adopt, modify, or decline a proposal.

Section 13. Frequently Asked Questions

13.1 Who is eligible for accommodations?

Any student with a documented disability that substantially limits one or more major life
activities may be eligible. Documentation must be current and provided by a qualified
professional. The office reviews each request on an individual basis. A diagnosis alone does
not automatically result in accommodations; the impact of the disability in the academic
setting is also considered.

13.2 How do I request accommodations?

Submit the Accommodation Request Form through the student portal. Attach your documentation.
The office will review your request and contact you to schedule an intake meeting. You do not
need to request accommodations before the semester begins, but early requests allow more time
for implementation.

13.3 How long does the review process take?

The office aims to review complete requests within 10 business days of receipt. If
documentation is incomplete or unclear, the office will contact you for additional
information. The timeline restarts once all materials are received.

13.4 Can I receive accommodations for online classes?

Yes. Many accommodations apply to online courses, including extended time on quizzes,
captioning for recorded lectures, and alternative formats for course materials. Discuss your
specific needs with your accessibility specialist.

13.5 Are accommodations retroactive?

No. Accommodations begin after your accommodation plan is approved and you have notified your
instructors. The office cannot provide retroactive accommodations for past assignments or
exams.

13.6 What if my instructor does not follow my accommodation plan?

Contact the office as soon as possible. The office will help resolve the issue with the
instructor. If the issue is not resolved informally, you may file a grievance under Section
11 of this handbook.

13.7 Do I need to request accommodations every semester?

No. Once your accommodation plan is approved, it remains in effect until you graduate, take a
leave of absence, or request changes. You are responsible for notifying your instructors each
semester that you are using accommodations.

13.8 Can I change my accommodation plan?

Yes. You may request changes at any time by contacting your accessibility specialist. Changes
may require updated documentation. The office will review requested changes and notify you of
the decision within 10 business days.

13.9 What if I am not satisfied with a decision about my accommodations?

You may discuss your concerns with your accessibility specialist or the Director of
Accessibility Resources. If the issue is not resolved, you may file a grievance under Section
11. You may also contact the U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights at any time.

13.10 Are accommodations confidential?

Yes. The office maintains all records as confidential. Information is shared only with your
written permission or as required by law. Instructors receive a notification letter that lists
your accommodations, but not your diagnosis or documentation.

Section 14. Glossary of Terms

14.1 Accommodation Plan: A written document listing the specific accommodations a student is
eligible to receive. The plan is developed in the intake meeting and updated as needed.

14.2 Accessibility Specialist: The staff member assigned to a student to coordinate
accommodations and provide support.

14.3 Auxiliary Aids and Services: Tools and supports that enable equal access, including
sign language interpreters, captioning, assistive technology, and note-taking services.

Renewal and Changes to Your Accommodations

Your approved accommodations are valid for the current semester as listed in this letter. If you wish to continue receiving accommodations in a future semester, you must request a renewal through the OAR Student Portal. Renewal requests should be submitted no later than the third week of the semester prior to the one in which you need accommodations. For example, if you need accommodations for the Fall semester, submit your renewal request by the third week of the Spring semester. This timeline allows OAR sufficient time to review your request and notify your instructors before the start of the term.

To request a change to your current accommodations, log in to the OAR Student Portal and complete the Accommodation Change Request form. Changes may include adding a new accommodation, modifying an existing one, or removing an accommodation that is no longer needed. Please note that any change to your accommodations requires a new review by OAR, and you may be asked to provide updated documentation if your request is based on a change in your condition or circumstances. You do not need to submit a full renewal request if you are only requesting a change; the change request form is sufficient.

If you are requesting a change because your current accommodations are not meeting your needs, please include a brief explanation in the form. OAR will review your request and respond within ten business days. If additional information is needed, an OAR staff member will contact you by email or phone. You may also request a meeting with your assigned accessibility coordinator to discuss your needs in more detail. Meetings can be scheduled through the OAR Student Portal or by calling the front desk.

If you believe your accommodations should be adjusted due to a temporary condition, such as an injury or a short-term medical issue, you may request a temporary accommodation modification. Temporary modifications are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are generally approved for a limited duration. You will need to provide documentation from a qualified professional that describes the temporary condition and its expected duration. Once the temporary modification expires, your original accommodations will automatically resume. You do not need to reapply for your original accommodations after a temporary modification ends.

If you are denied a renewal or a change to your accommodations, you may appeal the decision. Information about the appeals process is available on the OAR website under the Policies section. Appeals must be submitted in writing within fifteen business days of the denial notice. The appeal should include a statement explaining why you believe the decision was incorrect and any supporting documentation. A review committee will consider your appeal and provide a written decision within twenty business days of receiving it.

Important Reminders

- Accommodations are not retroactive. They begin on the effective date listed in this letter and apply only to assessments and course activities that occur on or after that date.
- You are responsible for requesting your accommodations each semester. Approval in one semester does not automatically carry over to the next.
- If you add a course after the start of the semester, your accommodations will apply to that course once the add is processed. Please allow up to five business days for your instructor to receive notification for a new course.
- If you drop a course, your accommodations for that course will end on the date the drop is processed. You do not need to notify OAR when you add or drop a course; the portal updates automatically.
- If your contact information changes, update it in the OAR Student Portal so that you continue to receive important communications.
